properties.line: Wichita Falls and Northwestern: Wichita Falls – Forgan
properties.speed_source: estimated: typical branch-line service of the era; unsourced

segments.note: Chartered 1906 (two companies: one for the 17-mile Wichita Falls-Red River stretch, another for the rest), built 1906-1909, with service to the Wellington branch beginning Nov 10, 1910 and the main line reaching Forgan, in the Oklahoma Panhandle, Nov 1, 1912 - 359.3 miles of track known as the 'Wichita Falls Route.' The original plan was a line north through Indian Territory to Englewood, KS, but the route was redirected through Frederick, Altus, Elk City, and Woodward to Forgan instead. The Missouri, Kansas and Texas Railway (Katy) bought the company's stock in 1911, but it continued operating separately until 1923. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: Consolidated into the Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railroad (the 'Katy') on April 1, 1923. Competition from cars and buses eroded the branch through the mid-20th century; the MKT never submitted this line to Amtrak in 1971. The Katy finally abolished all train service on the Northwestern District in January 1973 (the last clean-up train reached Wichita Falls Jan 27, 1973). Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: Service on the Altus-Wellington branch began Nov 10, 1910. Changed transportation conditions, competition from cars and buses, and the Katy's persistent financial troubles led to the branch's abandonment in 1958, 15 years before the rest of the Wichita Falls Route. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
